$comment: THE READ RECORD of slice s-12 of the 1985 rules (kb/Work PB5597; DESIGN-spec-conformance-review.md section 10.6): the reader's and the refuter's files and the flags the slice asked, verbatim, with the digest of each source. Written by audit_batch.py import-reads; read only through lineage_reads.load, the one normalization.

scope-1985: every Nucleus statement (and every module's statements, by its rules) whose sending and receiving items share storage while defined by different data description entries
a pointer to statements whose general rules make same-entry overlap undefined

evidence-1985.overlap by different entries: result und: not shown (no program can show an undefined result)
evidence-1985.pointer to per-statement rules: not shown (it imposes nothing of its own; each statement's rule is its own row)

citations.quote: the result of the execution of such a statement is undefined
citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.4.5 p1  (6.4.5 Overlapping Operands)  the text is in p1

cases.reason: Definitional flag: can a program show it? No. The paragraph's only requirement is 'the result of the execution of such a statement is undefined'; its second and third sentences point to the general rules of other statements. The earlier prose85 read classed both sentences NOT-NORMATIVE (refutation UPHELD). 2023 GR-14.6.10-1 repeats sentence 1, but an undefined result has no observable outcome to witness at 85, so the undefined-in-rule arm closes it.
cases.compiler-at-1985: not probed: an undefined result has no outcome a program can check
cases.needs: a signed derivation

derivation.names: the result of the execution of such a statement is undefined

citations.quote: may have single or multiple resultant identifiers
citations.check: OK  §2023:14.7.7 GR4  (Arithmetic statements)  the text is in GR4

cases.reason: The paragraph grants a form ('The ADD, COMPUTE, DIVIDE, MULTIPLY, and SUBTRACT statements may have multiple results'), so each of the five statements needs an accepted program. GR-14.7.7-4 states the grant, but its 85 cases (l1c04_arith_multiple_receivers, pb5386_arith_receiver_identified_at_store) write multiple receivers only for ADD, COMPUTE and MULTIPLY; DIVIDE appears only as GIVING ... REMAINDER and SUBTRACT not at all. Probe p01 runs all five at 85 (INTO/FROM/BY and GIVING forms) and each receiver gets its own result: ADD 011 021 031, SUB 010 020 030, MUL 020 040 060, DIV 010 020 030, DVG 020 020 020, SBG 049 049 049, CMP 021 021 021.
cases.class: other: the pointer states the grant but its 85 cases leave out SUBTRACT and DIVIDE
cases.needs: needs-own-witness: place p01 as the row's own 85 test
